`class ComputedSignal<T>`<br/>
**Extends:** [`Signal<T>`](/reference/signals/signal/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.signal` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [ComputedSignal.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/signal/ComputedSignal.java)

Read-only signal whose value comes from a function of other signals, computed again only after one of them changed.

## Description

A `ComputedSignal<T>` comes from `Signal.from(...)` or `map(...)`.
It computes its value on the first read, records the signals that the function reads with `get()`, and computes again only when one of them changed.
While nothing follows it, it computes on demand; once a listener or another derived signal follows it, it follows its own signals and notifies its listeners when its result changes (by `equals`).
`set(...)` and `reset()` throw an `IllegalStateException`: set the signals it reads instead.

<a id="ComputedSignal-method-isConstant"></a>

### isConstant

`boolean isConstant()` 

If `true`, the value never changes: the signal comes from `Signal.from(value)` with an expression that read no signal.
A node keeps a constant value as a plain value and does not follow it.

<a id="ComputedSignal-method-refresh"></a>

### refresh

`void refresh()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: A ComputedSignal cannot read itself while it computes its value, remove the read of this signal from its function

Computes the value again when a signal it read changed since the last computation.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` when the function reads the signal that it computes.
When the function throws, the exception goes to the caller and the next read computes again.

## Event details

<a id="ComputedSignal-event-onChange"></a>

### onChange

`this onChange(SignalListener<? super T> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Calls `listener` with the result after each change of the result, on the render thread, then returns this signal.
From the first listener on, the signal follows the signals it reads instead of computing on demand.

<small>`fluent` returns the instance, typed for chaining · `factory` creates an instance · `signal` also accepts a value that follows signals, as a signal, an expression or a lambda ([When does JOID compute this value again?](/use/learn/interactivity/signals/#ask-when-does-joid-compute-this-value-again)) · `hook` called by JOID, override it · `abstract` you implement it · `default` interface method with a body · `static` called on the class · `protected` visible to subclasses</small>
